'''Célio Fernando Baptista Haddad''' (born 5 December 1959) is a Brazilian biologist specializing in [[herpetology]], as well as a writer and professor.

He completed his undergraduate degree in [[Biology|biological sciences]] in 1982 at the [[University of Campinas]], where he also completed a master's degree in 1987 and a doctorate in [[ecology]] in 1991. He is a full professor in the Department of [[Zoology]] at [[São Paulo State University]] in Rio Claro and a full member of the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]]. He has won two [[Jabuti Prize]]s, the first in [[1993]] for the book ''[[História Natural da Serra do Japi]]'' and the second in [[2014]] for the book ''[[Guia dos Anfíbios da Mata Atlântica]]''.<ref name="abc"/>

He is a recognized zoologist specializing in the taxonomy, systematics, [[phylogenetics]], evolution, behavior, and conservation of [[anuran]]s. As of mid-2017, Haddad had been the author of the descriptions of more than 50 species of these animals.<ref name="abc">{{cite web|title=Célio Fernando Baptista Haddad|url=http://www.abc.org.br/membro/celio-fernando-baptista-haddad/|access-date=|date=|publisher=Academia Brasileira de Ciências - Membros|last=|first=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615232128/http://www.abc.org.br/membro/celio-fernando-baptista-haddad/|archive-date=2020-06-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Interesse em diversidade|url=https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/interesse-em-diversidade/|work=Revista Pesquisa Fapesp|date=2011|publisher=|last=Marques|first=Fabrício Marques|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615231812/https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/interesse-em-diversidade/|archive-date=2020-06-15}}</ref>

He coordinated a research group at UNESP studying the reproduction of the São Paulo tree frog (''[[Thoropa taophora]]'').<ref>{{cite web|last=Stam|first=Gilberto|url=https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/o-sapo-fiel-2/|title=O sapo fiel|date=September 2020|access-date=2023-09-29|website=revistapesquisa.fapesp.br|language=pt-br}}</ref>

In 2021, he participated in a study on amphibian reproductive modes, documenting 74 distinct forms known to science.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://agencia.fapesp.br/estudo-amplia-de-39-para-74-os-modos-de-reproducao-conhecidos-dos-anfibios-e-cria-nova-classificacao/37024|title=Estudo amplia de 39 para 74 os modos de reprodução conhecidos dos anfíbios e cria nova classificação|date=2021-10-08|access-date=2023-09-29|website=AGÊNCIA FAPESP|language=pt-BR}}</ref>
